data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims outstanding increased from GBP 87.761m at 1 January 2016 to GBP 111.871m at 31 December 2016. The syndicate recorded gross adverse prior-year development of GBP 18.75m (approximately 21.4% of opening gross reserves), driven by adverse claims development / large loss development and other factors (including foreign exchange and increased IBNR on live business). The largest concentrations of outstanding liabilities are Third Party liability (gross GBP 54.899m), Reinsurance acceptance (gross GBP 32.968m) and Accident & Health (gross GBP 20.034m), indicating the reserve pressures are most material in casualty-type and reinsurance-acceptance business.
raw_causal_phrases: Gross technical provisions have increased from GBP 87.8m to GBP 111.9m; this increase is driven by the provision of IBNR on the live business and partially offset by the reductions in legacy balances.

The Agency has seen continued favourable development on the RITC contracts written by the Syndicate. This is borne out by the reviews performed by the Actuarial Function as at 30th June 2016, 30th September 2016 and 31st December 2016.
2016 saw a small increase in the level of catastrophe losses for the market; notably the Fort McMurray wildfires and Hurricane Matthew, where the Syndicate had limited exposure.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding and gross prior-year movement taken from the Statement of Financial Position (Liabilities - Claims outstanding) and the Claims Outstanding reconciliation (Note 3) respectively. Exact textual description of the prior-year movement is not provided in prose; the numeric movement was taken from the Note 3 table row 'Claims incurred in prior underwriting year 18,750 (2,465) 16,285'. Claims development triangle present but OCR/extraction in the source appears corrupted and contains an aggregate 'Before 2012' column which was excluded - triangle development figures could not be reliably parsed. RITC / legacy references are present in narrative and may distort some development patterns.
